questions.prompt: What problem does Book Three address that Book Two leaves unfinished?
choices: How to increase raw output speed once routine exists
How to keep the work from being distorted by ego even after discipline is learned
How to stop all criticism from affecting the worker emotionally

explanation.gentle: Book Three starts after routine exists and asks what the work is serving.
explanation.direct: The final movement is about motive and allegiance, not about making the calendar even stricter.
explanation.competitive: You can win the schedule and still lose the work to vanity.

questions.prompt: Which description best fits the chapter's idea of the higher realm?
choices: A license to ignore ordinary craft because the work comes from a special source
A frame that treats the work as answering to something larger than ego or self-display
A promise that praise will feel satisfying enough once calling is discovered

explanation.gentle: The chapter uses larger language to move the self out of the center of the labor.
explanation.direct: The higher frame changes allegiance. It does not cancel discipline or guarantee emotional comfort.
explanation.competitive: This is about authority, not aura.

questions.prompt: A worker keeps the schedule faithfully but still uses each outcome to decide whether they are impressive enough. What would Book Three most likely say?
choices: They have learned routine but not yet reordered the work beyond ego
They should stop caring about quality so the self has less to lose
They need a more demanding calendar rather than a different frame

explanation.gentle: The chapter says showing up is not the last issue if the work is still being used as identity proof.
explanation.direct: Book Three focuses on possession and motive after discipline has already been established.
explanation.competitive: The calendar is not the problem if the ego still owns the artifact.

questions.prompt: Imani notices that her final presentation slide makes her look sharper but makes the recommendation less clear. Which response best matches the chapter?
choices: Keep the sharper slide because the worker's confidence is part of the message
Remove the flourish and keep the version that best serves the truth of the task
Delay the meeting until she feels completely pure in motive

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks the worker to serve the task instead of using it for self-decoration.
explanation.direct: Faithful delivery outranks ego polish once the work is treated as entrusted rather than possessed.
explanation.competitive: Cut the vanity and keep the truth.

questions.prompt: Which option shows a mistaken reading of the higher-realm idea?
choices: Treating the larger frame as a reason to become more exact and humble in the work
Treating calling language as permission to drift into vague uplift and weaker craft
Treating service as a way to lower the ego temperature around feedback

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that larger language becomes false if it weakens craft or flatters the self.
explanation.direct: Book Three rejects mystical inflation and chosen-artist theater. The bigger frame must stay answerable to discipline.
explanation.competitive: If the frame makes you airy and sloppy, ego has changed costumes.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter keep discipline in force instead of replacing it with inspiration or spiritual feeling?
choices: Because the higher frame is honest only if it increases humility, labor, and craft
Because spiritual language is useful only in corporate settings
Because discipline guarantees that praise and criticism will stop hurting

explanation.gentle: The book keeps the habit because a larger purpose should make the work cleaner, not softer.
explanation.direct: Book Three does not discard Book Two. It gives discipline a truer object and keeps craft standards severe.
explanation.competitive: The real frame pushes you lower into the work, not out of it.

questions.prompt: Lucas wants his capstone project to make the room notice how original he is. What response best fits the chapter?
choices: Ask what the project itself needs and cut elements that exist mainly to flatter the maker
Add even more cleverness so the approval he wants is secured before critique begins
Detach from all feedback because service means no longer listening to others at all

explanation.gentle: Book Three redirects the work toward the task instead of toward approval hunger.
explanation.direct: Service becomes concrete when it changes studio decisions and removes vanity-driven additions.
explanation.competitive: Make the piece answer its job, not your insecurity.

questions.prompt: Renee keeps asking whether a song will raise her status. What shift would Book Three most likely require?
choices: Treat the song as entrusted work and judge choices by faithful delivery instead of image gain
Stop caring about the song so status no longer matters
Wait for a stronger mystical sign before deciding how to record it

explanation.gentle: The chapter pushes the artist from self-branding toward stewardship of the work itself.
explanation.direct: The issue is not whether she values the song, but whether the song is being used to certify identity.
explanation.competitive: Move from aura management to clean delivery.

questions.prompt: Why does service steady the worker more than ambition does in this chapter?
choices: Because service makes criticism impossible to feel
Because service points outward to the task instead of letting praise, fear, and comparison rule interpretation
Because service removes the need for standards or competition entirely

explanation.gentle: Service helps because it keeps the work aimed at the task instead of at self-display.
explanation.direct: Ambition rises and falls with feedback, while stewardship gives the worker a more stable relation to praise and blame.
explanation.competitive: Service is harder for vanity to bribe.

questions.prompt: What closing change does the book ultimately ask of the worker?
choices: To become indifferent to craft because purpose now matters more than execution
To move the self beneath the work so faithful delivery matters more than self-glorification
To avoid all praise and criticism by withdrawing from public work

explanation.gentle: The book closes by reordering the self under the task rather than by erasing the self or softening the work.
explanation.direct: Faithful delivery becomes the final measure once ego is no longer the master of interpretation.
explanation.competitive: The endgame is custody, not image.
